findings.message: Shutdown checks use the orchestrator's branch rather than the target implementer's branch, allowing unreviewed worktree implementers to be terminated. The branch comes exclusively from git symbolic-ref in process.cwd(); the target is used only for its name. When the orchestrator remains on main while an implementer works on a feature branch in a worktree, lines 91–94 allow shutdown immediately without checking that feature's reviews. The repository explicitly supports parallel branches and worktree implementation in templates/skills/dev-team-task/SKILL.md and templates/agents/dev-team-drucker.md.

A matching sidecar filename permits shutdown before review findings have been routed and acknowledged. files.some() checks only a filename substring and .json suffix, then lines 108–110 allow shutdown without reading findings or acknowledgment state. A sidecar containing unresolved findings therefore passes immediately, contrary to templates/skills/dev-team-task/SKILL.md's requirement that implementers remain alive until all findings are routed and acknowledged. It also accepts unrelated prefix matches, such as a feat-123-test sidecar for branch feat/123.

The installed hook ignores its event input and therefore allows premature implementer shutdowns. templates/settings.json invokes the script without arguments, but line 26 reads only process.argv[2]. Claude Code supplies command-hook events through stdin ([hook reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-input-and-output)). Supplying a SendMessage shutdown event on stdin returned exit 0: input becomes {}, and the tool-name check exits before enforcement. The new tests pass JSON as an argument, masking this integration failure.
